sops.title: Camera Signal Loss Recovery
sops.condition: One or more inspection cameras shows no video feed on the vision controller display.

sops.title: Lighting Intensity Gradual Drift Below Setpoint
sops.condition: The ambient light sensor records a slow, continuous decline to below the 350-lux minimum threshold over the course of a shift, triggering a low-light advisory alarm.

sops.title: Instantaneous Lighting Failure Response
sops.condition: The ambient light sensor drops to zero or near-zero instantaneously within a single scan cycle, indicating a bulb burnout or LED driver failure rather than a gradual drift.

sops.title: Reject Gate Physical Jam Clearance
sops.condition: The reject gate actuator is energized and commanded to the reject position but the gate does not move and the gate position sensor reads zero displacement after 3 seconds.

sops.title: Reject Gate Delayed Actuation Response
sops.condition: The reject gate moves to the reject position but consistently takes more than 1.5 seconds after the trigger signal, causing parts to occasionally clear the gate before it closes fully.

sops.title: Excessive False Reject Rate Response
sops.condition: The vision system is flagging and diverting more than 5% of parts to the reject bin that quality sampling confirms are conforming to dimensional and surface specifications.

sops.title: High Defect Miss Rate Response
sops.condition: Post-process audit or customer feedback confirms that defective parts are passing through the vision station and receiving a PASS disposition, indicating the system is under-detecting flaws.

sops.title: Camera Thermal Warning Response
sops.condition: A camera body temperature sensor triggers a WARNING-level amber alarm indicating temperature above 55 degrees C but below the 70 degree C emergency shutdown threshold, with the system still running.

sops.title: Scheduled Camera Lens Cleaning
sops.condition: The vision controller triggers an 8-hour interval lens contamination flag, or an operator observes smearing or hazing on live camera images consistent with oil mist or coolant overspray on the lens.

sops.title: Lighting Diffusion Filter Replacement
sops.condition: Scheduled 500-hour PM interval is reached or the lighting uniformity sensor triggers a diffusion degradation alarm indicating non-uniform illumination across the inspection zone.

sops.title: Reject Gate Actuator Lubrication
sops.condition: Scheduled weekly PM task for lubricating the reject gate pneumatic actuator rod and pivot bearings is due, or an operator reports audible squealing or grinding from the gate mechanism.

sops.title: Vision System Full Calibration
sops.condition: Scheduled 30-day calibration PM interval is reached or a calibration-due alarm is displayed on the vision controller, requiring the full calibration sequence with the reference target board.

sops.title: Camera Field-of-View Alignment Verification
sops.condition: Scheduled bi-weekly alignment verification is due or the vision controller reports an alignment drift alarm indicating the active field of view has shifted from the nominal center position.

sops.title: Vision Enclosure Air Filter Replacement
sops.condition: Scheduled monthly PM is due or the enclosure HVAC pressure differential sensor triggers a clog alarm indicating restricted airflow through the inlet filter.

sops.title: Reject Gate Actuator Pneumatic Seal Replacement
sops.condition: Scheduled annual PM is due or a slow pneumatic leakdown is audible at the reject gate actuator body, indicating worn or failed internal seals.

sops.title: Vision Station Lockout-Tagout Procedure
sops.condition: Any task requiring physical entry into the inspection enclosure or hands-on work involving electrical, pneumatic, or mechanical components of the vision station.

sops.title: Lens Cleaner Solvent Spill Response
sops.condition: Lens cleaning solvent or isopropyl alcohol is spilled within or immediately adjacent to the vision station enclosure, creating a slip hazard or chemical exposure risk.

sops.title: Vision Station Emergency Stop Activation
sops.condition: Any unsafe condition, uncontrolled mechanical motion, personnel hazard, smoke, or imminent equipment damage is observed at the vision station requiring immediate cessation of all motion.

sops.title: Vision Station Startup Sequence
sops.condition: Beginning of production shift or return from any planned downtime requiring the vision station to be brought from a fully de-energized state to production-ready operation.

sops.title: Vision Station End-of-Shift Shutdown
sops.condition: End of the production shift or start of planned downtime requiring orderly shutdown of the vision station from production-running state to fully de-energized.

sops.title: First Article Inspection Program Setup
sops.condition: A new part number or tooling changeover requires selection of the correct vision inspection program and a golden-part verification pass before production is released to run.

sops.title: Golden Part Start-of-Shift Verification Run
sops.condition: Scheduled start-of-shift or post-maintenance check requiring the certified golden-part sample set to be run through the active inspection program to confirm current detection accuracy before production begins.

incidents.text: Screen went blank on camera 3 right after startup, no picture at all. Line 3 was sitting dead for about 10 minutes before anyone noticed parts were running through unchecked. Had to call it out over the radio. — D. Kowalski, 2nd shift

Operator at the south bay reported one of the monitors on the inspection unit just went dark mid-run. Parts were still moving on the belt but nothing was being checked upstream. Had to halt the line. — M. Torres, 1st shift

After the lunch break the whole right-side display on the unit by the loading dock came back with nothing on it. Kept blinking, no image at all. Someone had to run product blind until the vision tech got there. — J. Park, 3rd shift

Lights inside the inspection zone looked washed out and kind of yellowish, noticeably dimmer than normal. It was fine at 6 AM but by noon you could barely see the part surface on the monitor. Crept up on us slow. — R. Singh, 1st shift

The system kept throwing up a yellow banner — not the red alarm, just a yellow advisory — and the ring lights were obviously less bright than last week. Took most of the morning to get bad enough to notice. Definitely not sudden. — C. Barba, 2nd shift

Lights just cut out. One second they were full brightness over the nest, the next second pitch black. No dimming beforehand, just gone. Had to shout to get everybody to stop the line immediately. — A. Duda, 2nd shift

Everything went dark on the camera side right in the middle of a production run. Absolutely no warning, no flicker. Total blackout over the inspection area in an instant. Nothing gradual about it. — T. Nguyen, 1st shift

The arm that kicks the bad ones into the reject chute just wouldn't budge. You could hear it trying — thumping — but nothing moved. Parts were piling up past the gate and going into the good bin. — B. Koonce, 3rd shift

Reject chute door was stuck completely solid. Heard one hard thump then nothing. Tried to push it by hand and there was something wedged in the mechanism — wouldn't shift at all. — L. Martinez, 1st shift
The divert flap froze up in the middle of a cycle. The controller HMI showed it as active but you could see with your own eyes it wasn't going anywhere. Completely immobilized. — S. Patel, 2nd shift

Gate's moving but it's lazy about it. Takes a beat too long after the reject signal and some of the flagged parts are already past it by the time the flap swings over. Nothing stuck, just slow. — M. Chen, 1st shift

The kicker arm actuates fine — it does eventually swing — but there's this obvious lag between the alarm and the physical movement. Some rejects are ending up in the good bin because it doesn't get there in time. — P. Okafor, 2nd shift

Quality pulled 30 parts out of the red bin at the end of the shift and 28 of them checked out perfectly good. Vision system's being way too jumpy on the surface check. Good parts going in the scrap pile. — D. Stein, 1st shift

Scrap rate spiked to something insane this morning but when we mic'd the parts ourselves they were all in spec. The machine is flagging everything that comes through. Good product getting diverted. — C. Walsh, 2nd shift

Reject count was almost 1 in 5 today on line 2. Ran a bunch of them by hand inspection and they all pass visual and dimensional. The vision box is seeing things that aren't there. — T. Adeyemi, 3rd shift

Found a cracked housing in a finished shipping box that should have been pulled at the camera check. That part definitely went through — it had the PASS label on it. Something's not triggering on the bad ones. — K. Brown, QA

Customer called in a complaint. Scratched parts showed up in their incoming inspection, and our system had them stamped PASS and shipped. Defects are getting through the camera station without being flagged. — R. Cho, quality coordinator

A yellow alarm came up on the vision controller box — something about camera temperature. System was still fully running, nothing tripped or stopped. Just that amber warning sitting there. — F. DiMaggio, 2nd shift

Got a blinking amber on the panel at the inspection station on the north side. Nothing stopped, cameras were still live and producing images. Tech said it was running warm but hadn't hit the critical cutoff yet. — B. Otieno, 1st shift

System threw a focus error but the part design hasn't changed. Looking at the monitor you can see a smear over the center of the image — looks like oil mist or something on the glass in front of the lens. — A. Rossi, 1st shift

Camera 2 on the unit by the south wall has been showing a milky haze for a couple hours. Parts look blurry on-screen. Same thing happened last month after the press next door had a coolant overspray incident. — H. Kim, 2nd shift

Light over inspection zone 2 looks uneven — super bright right in the center and noticeably dark around the edges. Been like that for a few shifts, not totally out, just a patchy spread. — O. Bell, 1st shift
Every part that sits in the nest looks like it has a shadow on one side in the camera image. Ring light isn't spreading evenly anymore. Pretty sure the diffuser is worn out. — G. Cruz, 3rd shift
Reject arm is making a grinding squeak on every single cycle. Moves fine, no hesitation, but the noise is getting louder each shift. Been building all week. — P. Hadley, 2nd shift
Gate is squealing on every stroke out here on line 4. Maintenance walked by and said it's overdue for grease — nothing mechanically broken but it sounds like metal on metal. — N. Watts, 1st shift

PM calendar says calibration was due last Tuesday. Nobody got to it during that shift and it's been sitting past the window ever since. Still running product through but we're overdue. — J. Ferris, process tech

Controller had a banner on it when I powered up this morning that said something like CALIBRATION DUE. Been about a month since the last one, or maybe longer. Just sitting there on the screen at startup. — W. Osei, 1st shift
Monthly PM checklist came back and it flagged the calibration as overdue by 6 days. Nothing crashed or alarmed hard but the tracking sheet shows we blew past the interval. — C. Lin, maintenance

Parts are consistently poking out to the left side of the camera frame on camera 2. Looks like the view has drifted since sometime last week. Not throwing an alarm yet but something's visibly off-center. — T. Russo, 1st shift

Inspection images look off to me — the feature we're supposed to be checking is halfway out of frame on one camera. My guess is the cleaning crew bumped the mount over the weekend. — S. Oluwafemi, 2nd shift

Controller inside the enclosure on the east line tripped a high-temp advisory. Stuck my hand near the intake vent and airflow is barely there — feels completely restricted compared to normal. — B. Huang, maintenance

Enclosure has been running noticeably hotter than usual all shift. The vent grille on the side is pulling almost nothing. Filter in there looks like it's never been touched. — D. McAllister, 1st shift

There's a hissing sound coming from right around the reject arm cylinder. Air is bleeding out somewhere on the actuator block. Gate still cycles but pressure feels low and it's definitely slower than it should be. — R. Petrov, 2nd shift

Slow air bleed on the actuator body on the reject gate — not a big rupture, just a steady hiss you can hear if you stand close. Gate's working for now but it's been getting worse over the past few days. — M. Jensen, maintenance

Need to go inside the enclosure to swap out a camera mount bracket. Walked up and the conveyor was still enabled and no lock was on the disconnect. Nobody had isolated it before starting. — P. Amara, maintenance

Tech had their hand right next to the camera bracket for a lens swap and the station hadn't been properly de-energized before they went in. Shift supervisor caught it and stopped them immediately. — Y. Tanaka, area supervisor

Knocked over a small bottle of lens cleaner while prepping for the PM — it went right off the shelf and splashed onto the conveyor belt below the camera mount. Might have gotten into the belt drive area. — C. Santos, 1st shift

IPA spilled on the floor right at the base of the vision stand during a lens cleaning. Not a huge amount but the floor is slippery and the spill is sitting close to the power strip and the cable tray. — A. Mehta, 2nd shift
Part went sideways on the belt and was about to get dragged up into the camera frame mount at high speed. Hit the red mushroom without thinking. Whole line stopped instantly. — L. Thomas, 1st shift
Robot arm on the upstream welding cell swung way too close to the camera enclosure on the traverse. Smacked the e-stop before it could make contact. Everything halted. — O. Rivera, 2nd shift
Saw what looked like smoke or haze coming out from behind the vision controller panel. Didn't wait around, just hit the mushroom on the front and stepped back. — B. Park, 3rd shift

Came in at 6 AM for day shift and the station was completely dark — nobody from nights had powered it up before they left. Had to walk through the whole boot process before we could start running parts. — D. Kowalski, 1st shift

Coming back after the long weekend, everything at the vision station was fully cold — power had been cut at the panel for the holiday shutdown. Took longer than a normal morning start to get it back online from scratch. — J. Ito, maintenance

End of 2nd shift and the cameras were still live, system running, when 3rd shift showed up. Nobody had gone through the power-down steps before leaving. Third shift didn't know what state anything was in. — T. Cruz, 2nd shift

Station was left fully on over the weekend. Came in Monday and the controller had been running with no product for two days straight. Trying to get better about the end-of-week power-off routine. — S. Williams, maintenance

Switched over to the new bracket part number after the morning break but the vision box was still on the old housing recipe. First dozen-plus pieces ran through on the wrong inspection program before anyone caught it. — M. Baxter, 1st shift

Tooling change-over right after lunch. Nobody loaded the new inspection recipe and the system sat there passing parts it wasn't even looking at correctly for those dimensions. Only figured it out when quality walked by. — C. Dube, process tech

Start-of-shift check this morning — ran the known-bad part with the surface scratch through and it came back with a green PASS. That's supposed to be an automatic reject. Something's wrong with how it's reading right now. — R. Andersen, 1st shift

Weekly verification run with the certified sample kit after maintenance was done on the station. One of the gold pieces — the one with the known edge chip — went through and didn't get flagged as a reject. Shift lead stopped the line right away. — O. Eze, quality tech

Post-PM check using the reference samples. The sample with the subsurface void that's supposed to always trigger a reject came through clean with no alarm. Couldn't release the line until we figured out what changed. — F. Nakamura, process engineer

Images from the top camera look like they shifted overnight — the feature we measure for the edge distance is clipped on the right side of every frame. No alarm fired but inspection results were all over the place at startup. — B. Reyes, 1st shift
